source.author: cic
source.text: quorum ego orationes si, ut spero, ita expressero virtutibus utens illorum omnibus, id est sententiis et earum figuris et rerum ordine, verba persequens eatenus, ut ea non abhorreant a more nostroquae si e Graecis omnia conversa non erunt, tamen ut generis eiusdem sint, elaboravimus, erit regula, ad quam eorum dirigantur orationes qui Attice volent dicere.
source.text_original: quorum ego orationes si, ut spero, ita expressero virtutibus utens illorum omnibus, id est sententiis et earum figuris et rerum ordine, verba persequens eatenus, ut ea non abhorreant a more nostro—quae si e Graecis omnia conversa non erunt, tamen ut generis eiusdem sint, elaboravimus—, erit regula, ad quam eorum dirigantur orationes qui Attice volent dicere.
source.text_english: If I shall, as I hope, have rendered their speeches in such a way, using all their excellences—namely, their thought and the figures of thought and the arrangement of matter—while pursuing the words only so far that they do not depart from our custom, and which, if not all translated from the Greeks, shall nevertheless be of the same kind, we shall have established a standard to which the speeches of those who wish to speak Atticly may be directed.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: rursumque in calce sermonis: quorum ego, ait, orationes si, ut spero, ita expressero uirtutibus utens illorum omnibus, id est sententiis et earum figuris et rerum ordine, uerba persequens eatenus, ut ea non abhorreant a more nostro, quae si e Graecis omnia conuersa non erunt, tamen, ut generis eiusdem sint, elaborauimus et cetera.
reuse.text_original: rursumque in calce sermonis: quorum ego, ait, orationes si, ut spero, ita expressero uirtutibus utens illorum omnibus, id est sententiis et earum figuris et rerum ordine, uerba persequens eatenus, ut ea non abhorreant a more nostro, quae si e Graecis omnia conuersa non erunt, tamen, ut generis eiusdem sint, elaborauimus (et cetera).
reuse.text_english: and again at the end of the discourse: of these, he says, if I shall have set forth their speeches, as I hope, using all their virtues, that is, their thoughts and the figures of those thoughts and the order of the matter, pursuing the words only so far that they do not depart from our custom, in such a way that, although all things are not translated from the Greeks, still, so that they may be of the same kind, we have taken pains, and so on.
